How testing and attribution are verified

Each implementation has its own creator declarations, code contributors, source revision, dependencies, and test reports.

GitHub verifies each registered workflow, job outcome, and source revision. Reviewers declare the test level, platform, protocol scope, and dependency revisions in the registry. Current reports match the synchronized revisions. Source-integrity checks confirm code assembly.

Earlier evidence keeps its original citation. “No report” means a verified report has yet to be registered for that test level. Creator declarations include an attribution source. Code contributors come from GitHub-linked authors in mapped file histories. Shared files can include contributions to other features.
